decision_reason: Hold pending source-to-service parity. California's live CalCAT page reports a July 16, 2026 release, serves combined COVID-19, influenza, and RSV forecasts, and links this repository as CalCAT Open Source; the repository README still describes a COVID-only Shiny application, and the last code push was January 23, 2024. The official link establishes a relationship but not that this repository is the current source for the full operational service.

government_provenance.note: The California Department of Public Health operates the current CalCAT service and its footer directly links to this repository as the open-source project.

public_source.note: The canonical StateOfCalifornia/CalCAT repository is public and exposes source files and history.

eligible_license.note: GitHub identifies the repository license as MIT; the repository LICENSE is the source grant.

primary_evidence.note: The current official service describes combined COVID-19, influenza, and RSV burden and links the repository, but the linked repository README describes a COVID-only application; the source-to-current-service lineage is not established.

metadata_note: Open-source year is based on the repository's first MIT-license addition, commit e94e8ba99a1b5f916aab65283e5d61fe254081f7 (2020-06-29); the current service-to-repository parity remains unresolved.

decision_reason: Hold as an early research demonstrator: NIST describes the repository as an experimental testbed and demonstration probes; the public repository has no tagged release, and neither a government deployment nor documented independent reuse was evidenced. It therefore does not yet meet the baseline maturity/notability screen despite passing the four source checks.

government_provenance.note: NIST identifies the ITL AI Program research team as developing these evaluation probes and links to this repository.

public_source.note: The canonical usnistgov repository is public and contains the probe demonstrator source and documentation.

eligible_license.note: The repository license states NIST federal-employee work is not copyrighted in the United States under 17 U.S.C. §105 and expressly grants use, copying, modification, derivative works, and distribution, subject to notice and disclaimer.

primary_evidence.note: NIST's official project page links this repository and describes its evaluation probes and experimental testbed; the project is dated as starting in April 2026.

agency: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), Information Technology Laboratory AI Program
license: NIST software public-domain/reuse grant (17 U.S.C. §105; express permission subject to notice and disclaimer)

decision_reason: CISA and Idaho National Laboratory identify CSET as a specific cybersecurity assessment tool; CISA distributes it with installation and user guidance. The source is public, the repository grants MIT terms (with other separately licensed notices identified), and the 2019 public GitHub source is the earliest defensible year for licensed code in this repository.

government_provenance.note: CISA describes CSET as a stand-alone desktop assessment application; the repository README identifies CISA and Idaho National Laboratory as its developers.

public_source.note: The canonical CISA repository is public and contains application source, installation guidance, user guides, and release links.

eligible_license.note: The project License.txt grants MIT rights; the README also identifies Apache-2.0 components and says LGPL build dependencies are acquired separately and are not distributed. The License.txt history first records the MIT grant in a 2018-11-12 commit (https://github.com/cisagov/cset/commit/4f9f78597fdcf9ad5322d9cf45c9e940505b4587); the public repository was created in 2019, so 2019 is the earliest defensible public licensed-source year.

primary_evidence.note: The README states that CISA and INL develop CSET, describes its cybersecurity assessment purpose, and provides installation and release guidance, directly tying this code to the named government product.

agency: Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), with Idaho National Laboratory (INL; Battelle Energy Alliance)

decision_reason: The New York State Senate's OpenLegislation is a live legislative information API used by the Senate website and documented by the Senate as an open-source project. The public source and repository licensing policy are directly verifiable; its agency-distributed service and developer documentation meet the notability baseline. The official 2010 retrospective reports open-source snapshots in 2009 but does not identify their license terms; 2010 is the earliest preserved BSD/GPL grant.

government_provenance.note: The Senate's own announcement describes its OpenLegislation service, says the code snapshots were released open source in 2009, and describes moving day-to-day development to GitHub in 2010.

public_source.note: The canonical nysenate repository is public and contains the API implementation and documentation; its README identifies the project as from the New York State Senate.

eligible_license.note: The Senate licensing notice provides BSD or GPL version 3 for Senate-created code and specifies that pre-existing components retain their stated licensing conditions. The first preserved repository LICENSE commit is dated 2010-08-13 (https://github.com/nysenate/OpenLegislation/commit/d4cb1ce98448b3e8c7cd927ab100650226975b64); although the Senate 2010 announcement retrospectively reports open-source code snapshots in 2009, it does not name their license terms, so 2010 is the first defensible licensed-source year.

primary_evidence.note: The official New York State Senate legislation API is the deployed OpenLegislation service; the Senate announcement links the service and the source project and documents its public release.

license: BSD OR GPL-3.0 for Senate-created code; component-specific terms may apply

decision_reason: StateCU is a named State of Colorado consumptive-use model with official software releases, user documentation, developer resources, and a public source repository. The official product page directly links this GPL-licensed source and describes its use in state water projects, satisfying the agency-distributed software pathway.

government_provenance.note: The official OpenCDSS page identifies StateCU as the State of Colorado's consumptive-use model, links official state releases and this repository, and names CWCB/DWR developers in its product documentation.

public_source.note: The public OpenCDSS repository contains StateCU source code, tests, documentation, and release history.

eligible_license.note: The repository and official product page identify GPL version 3 or later. The license file is present from the initial repository history, with a 2017-01-03 commit (https://github.com/OpenCDSS/cdss-app-statecu-fortran/commit/07d280f2db2146149575ce0f0258549e6488e635), supporting 2017 as the earliest defensible licensed-source year.

primary_evidence.note: The product page provides current official StateCU downloads, user manuals, developer documentation, and the direct link to its source; it describes the model's Colorado CDSS role.

agency: State of Colorado — Colorado Water Conservation Board and Division of Water Resources (Colorado's Decision Support Systems)

decision_reason: StateDMI is an official Colorado CDSS data-management application with current state software downloads and user/developer documentation. government_provenance.note: The official OpenCDSS product page provides official StateDMI releases and identifies the tool's role preparing Colorado CDSS model inputs; it links the repository and documentation.

public_source.note: The OpenCDSS repository is public and contains the StateDMI application, tests, and documentation.

eligible_license.note: The repository and official product page identify GPL version 3 or later. primary_evidence.note: The state page names StateDMI, provides official downloads, manuals, GPL terms, and a direct source link; its documentation states the software automates preparation of StateCU and StateMod inputs.

agency: State of Colorado — Colorado Water Conservation Board and Division of Water Resources (Colorado's Decision Support Systems)

decision_reason: StateMod is the State of Colorado's water-allocation model, with official releases supporting state projects, user manuals, developer documentation, and a public source repository. government_provenance.note: The official product page identifies StateMod as the State of Colorado's water-allocation model, provides official state releases, lists state DWR/CWCB development contacts, and links this source repository.

public_source.note: The public OpenCDSS repository contains the StateMod Fortran model source, tests, and documentation.

primary_evidence.note: The product page provides official StateMod downloads, the user manual, developer documentation, licensing terms, and the direct source link; it describes StateMod's water-allocation function.

agency: State of Colorado — Colorado Water Conservation Board and Division of Water Resources (Colorado's Decision Support Systems)

decision_reason: TSTool is a named Colorado CDSS utility for time-series and related data processing, with official state releases, training and user documentation, and a public source repository. government_provenance.note: The official product page describes TSTool's role in the Colorado CDSS workflow, provides official state releases, training and documentation, identifies GPL terms, and links its source.

public_source.note: The public OpenCDSS repository contains the TSTool application source and documentation.

eligible_license.note: The repository and official product page identify GPL version 3 or later. primary_evidence.note: The state product page directly ties TSTool to the Colorado CDSS, links its official distribution and user/developer documentation, and identifies its relationship to StateCU and StateMod.

product_identity: TSTool time-series and data processing application
agency: State of Colorado — Colorado Water Conservation Board and Division of Water Resources (Colorado's Decision Support Systems)

decision_reason: The repository is the source for EPA's CTX Hazard API, a documented live federal service for human and ecotoxicology data. EPA's official API guide and data-domain page identify the service and its underlying ToxValDB/ToxRefDB sources. The source is public and the current MIT grant was added in 2025; 2025 is therefore the first defensible year of licensed code, not the repository's earlier creation date.

government_provenance.note: EPA's official data-domain page names the Hazard API, describes its human/ecotoxicology data, and links its documentation; the repository README says this API originates from EPA CCTE and points to EPA guidance.

public_source.note: The canonical USEPA repository is public and contains the REST API implementation, deployment files, and documentation links.

eligible_license.note: The current LICENSE.md grants the MIT License to the software. GitHub file history shows this MIT license was first added on 2025-04-15 (https://github.com/USEPA/ccte-api-hazard/commit/0625256d928148c6bb856e3e4651121b224ecb3a); because earlier public repository code lacked this grant, 2025 is the first defensible year of licensed source.

primary_evidence.note: EPA's API documentation is linked by the repository README and describes official CTX API access; the accompanying official data-domain page specifically identifies the Hazard endpoint and its toxicology databases.

product_identity: Computational Toxicology and Exposure (CTX) Hazard API
agency: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, Office of Research and Development, Center for Computational Toxicology and Exposure

decision_reason: Analytics.usa.gov is GSA's live dashboard and source project for Digital Analytics Program reporting across U.S. federal agency websites. GSA documents the production API and the repository as an open-source example. The repository's public-domain/CC0 statement first appears in January 2015, supporting 2015 as the first defensible year of licensed public code.

government_provenance.note: GSA's official open-source examples page directly lists analytics.usa.gov as a site with an open-source repository; GSA's DAP API documentation ties the dashboard and its reports to the federal Digital Analytics Program.

public_source.note: The 18F repository is public and contains the dashboard site source and project documentation.

eligible_license.note: The project license places U.S. government work in the U.S. public domain and waives worldwide copyright and related rights through CC0 1.0. Its LICENSE.md history begins with a 2015-01-14 licensing commit (https://github.com/18F/analytics.usa.gov/commit/4a9d0a5ed26da83c168e7300faeddeaab35ca6cc), supporting 2015 as the first defensible licensed-source year; listed vendor assets have separate licenses.

primary_evidence.note: GSA's DAP documentation describes the analytics.usa.gov reports and API as federal-agency traffic data, providing direct evidence of an operational government service and its purpose.

agency: U.S. General Services Administration, Technology Transformation Services, Digital Analytics Program
license: Public domain in the United States; CC0 1.0 Universal waiver worldwide (project code; vendor assets separately licensed)

decision_reason: Hold pending a repository-scope license determination. The main project LICENSE.txt grants Apache-2.0, but it expressly carves out JA4+ algorithms used by the Zeek and Arkime components and points to a FoxIO license limited to non-commercial use and distribution. CISA's product relationship and public source are established, but it is unclear whether the restricted components are included in the offered repository/product or separable from the cataloged software; do not treat the full product as Apache-only or assign a licensed-source year until resolved.

government_provenance.note: CISA describes Malcolm as its no-cost open-source network-traffic analysis tool for OT/ICS; the CISA Malcolm page and public cisagov repository provide current stewardship and deployment guidance. The repo names Battelle Energy Alliance/INL as author/copyright holder.

public_source.note: The canonical cisagov repository is public and exposes the network-monitoring suite source, installation and deployment docs, and releases.

eligible_license.note: The project LICENSE grants Apache-2.0 to the main project, but notes that JA4+ algorithms used by Zeek and Arkime components have separate licensing requirements. The linked FoxIO License restricts use and distribution to non-commercial purposes (https://github.com/FoxIO-LLC/ja4/blob/main/LICENSE); the boundary of those components in the cataloged source is not established. Apache clarification first appears in a 2023-07-06 commit (https://github.com/cisagov/Malcolm/commit/fb928a5cfec11a0cfe2fe21bea11d05507b0bcae), but an open-source year for the complete package remains unresolved.

primary_evidence.note: CISA's official Malcolm resource describes the tool's network traffic analysis role for OT/ICS, and CISA directs users to the software and documentation; the product has official user guidance and versioned releases.

agency: Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA; Battelle Energy Alliance/Idaho National Laboratory copyright and authorship)
license: Apache-2.0 for the main project; JA4+ components subject to separate FoxIO non-commercial terms

decision_reason: Hold pending rights/scope confirmation for the original trec_eval code. NIST's 2024 LICENSE.md gives broad reuse rights for NIST-developed modifications, but states that code through version 9 is copyright Chris Buckley; the core trec_eval.c still carries a research-only, non-commercial permission notice. The repository is public and directly associated with NIST TREC, but the current top-level notice does not clearly resolve commercial use of the original code, so no eligible-license result or first licensed-source year can be assigned.

government_provenance.note: NIST's official TREC site identifies trec_eval as its evaluation software; the current repository is in the usnistgov organization and its README identifies the Text Retrieval Conference evaluation use.

public_source.note: The canonical NIST repository is public and exposes the evaluation code, documentation, and release history.

eligible_license.note: The NIST grant permits reuse of NIST-developed software and modifications, but the same notice attributes original code through version 9 to Chris Buckley. The core source file separately restricts use and modification to research, non-commercial purposes (https://github.com/usnistgov/trec_eval/blob/main/trec_eval.c); this apparent scope conflict needs rights-holder clarification. LICENSE.md itself was added 2024-01-15 (https://github.com/usnistgov/trec_eval/commit/f222e22fb8c50c81b106e5d143d80a381ff7028e), but no defensible year of fully eligible licensed source is established.

primary_evidence.note: NIST's official TREC page documents trec_eval as the evaluation program for the conference and links project information; the repository README describes the software's identity and use.

agency: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), Information Technology Laboratory; original code by Chris Buckley
license: NIST reuse grant for NIST-developed modifications; original code carries a research/non-commercial restriction pending scope clarification
